real_conflicts: The proposal to 'replace the heavy geometric font with a distorted sans-serif' (Typography Integration) threatens the production-level finish. Distorting the typeface risks making the poster look like a low-resolution digital glitch rather than a sophisticated print piece. The current sharpness of the text provides the necessary 'control' to contrast with the 'release' of the background; degrading the text quality undermines the craft.

The proposal to 'increase the opacity of the figure to make it a dominant visual force' (Composition Hierarchy) risks creating a muddy, low-contrast mess. If the figure becomes too opaque, it will clash with the white text, destroying the legibility and the atmospheric depth. The current 'ghostly' opacity is a deliberate craft choice that allows the text to float in the 'air'.
accepted: The proposal to 'deepen the background gradient to a rich, moody charcoal or deep violet-black' (Color Atmosphere Craft) is essential. The current background is too washed out and lacks the 'weight' required by the title. A deeper tonal range will provide the necessary contrast for the white text to pop.

The proposal to 'apply a subtle noise texture or grain overlay' (Color Atmosphere Craft) is accepted. This will unify the digital text with the abstract background, removing the sterile 'default template' feel and adding the requested tactile, physical finish.
concession: I concede that the current background gradient is too faint and the faint grid lines are gratuitous digital artifacts that should be removed. I also concede that the text needs to interact more with the atmosphere, but this should be achieved through texture and lighting, not by distorting the typeface itself.
compromise: We will deepen the background to a rich, dark violet-black to increase emotional gravity and legibility. We will apply a unified film grain texture over the entire composition (text and background) to give it a physical, tactile quality. We will remove the faint grid lines. The text will remain sharp and geometric to represent 'control,' but the grain and deep shadows will allow the 'body' to feel like it is emerging from the darkness behind the letters, creating the tension between control and release without sacrificing legibility.
nonnegotiable: The text must remain sharp, high-contrast, and legible. We cannot sacrifice the 'production-level finish' of the typography for the sake of abstract effects; the text must anchor the composition with authority.
